records.claimSummary: The orchestrator publishes a StockReserved event to the message broker.
records.conditionSummary: Only once both the ledger reservation and the pricing step succeed.
records.mustConvey: only after both reserve and pricing succeed
records.bindingReason: Publishing StockReserved is false when either the reservation or the pricing step fails.
records.notes: Intra-sentence. Edges u3_n5->u3_n7 and u3_n6->u3_n7 are labelled 'if successful', which also conveys it; u3_n7->u3_n8 makes it linked.

records.claimSummary: The orchestrator asks the stock ledger to reserve the requested quantity.
records.conditionSummary: If the ledger cannot reserve the full quantity, the whole order is rejected; never a partial reservation.
records.mustConvey: all-or-nothing: whole order rejected if full quantity unavailable, no partial reservation
records.bindingReason: The reserve-request sentence stays true; the all-or-nothing rule is an outcome that must be recorded somewhere.
records.notes: g2 takeaway 'manages atomic stock reservations' judged recognisable for all-or-nothing. u3_n5 is also linked to u3_n9 ('if ledger cannot reserve').

records.claimSummary: The ledger reserves the requested stock for the order.
records.conditionSummary: A reservation not confirmed within 15 minutes is released and the stock becomes available again.
records.bindingReason: The reservation still happens; the 15-minute release bounds how long it holds.
records.notes: g2 takeaway ('with a timeout') and u3_a1 ('time-based release') lack the 15-minute value, so not carriers. u3_n10 is joined only to u3_n3 (orchestrator label) via 'timeout condition'.

records.claimSummary: The feed adapter wraps supplier API calls in the retry helper.
records.conditionSummary: At most 5 attempts per delivery; backoff 2 s doubling capped at 60 s; after 5th failure, published to inventory.dlq for staff review.
records.mustConvey: max 5 attempts; 2 s start, doubling, 60 s cap; then inventory.dlq
records.bindingReason: 'Calls are retried' stays true; the policy bounds it.

records.claimSummary: Supplier calls are retried under the retry policy.
records.conditionSummary: Retries apply only to supplier calls; reservations are never retried automatically and failures return an error to the caller.
records.mustConvey: retries only for supplier calls; reservations never auto-retried (error returned to caller)
records.bindingReason: The retry policy statement is true for supplier calls; the scope note prevents over-generalisation.
records.notes: u7_n3 names supplier API calls but not the 'only' / reservations-never-retried part; g6 takeaway is silent; no arrows inside g6.

records.claimSummary: The adapter converts each delivery into a restock and asks the ledger to record it.
records.conditionSummary: A delivery it cannot parse is logged and skipped, not retried.
records.mustConvey: unparsable deliveries are logged and skipped (not retried)
records.bindingReason: 'Each delivery is converted into a restock' is false for deliveries that cannot be parsed.
records.notes: g4 takeaway '... logging unparsable data' judged recognisable but weak on 'skipped'. u5_n5 links to u5_n10 ('Handle Unparsable Delivery'), a label I did not count as a carrier on its own.

records.claimSummary: Dead-lettered deliveries are reviewed by staff in the admin UI.
records.conditionSummary: They are only found when someone opens the admin UI; nothing alerts when inventory.dlq fills.
records.mustConvey: no alerting on inventory.dlq; found only by manually opening the admin UI
records.bindingReason: Staff do review the DLQ in the UI; the lack of alerting is an operational gap, not a falsifier.

records.claimSummary: The ledger is the only writer of stock; others go through it.
records.conditionSummary: Orchestrator and adapter can change the same product at once; consistency relies on a row lock unmeasured under peak load.
records.mustConvey: concurrent changes rely on a DB row lock whose behaviour at peak load is unmeasured
records.bindingReason: Single-writer remains true; the unmeasured lock is a risk caveat.
records.notes: Attachment of u49 to a specific claim is debatable (could also qualify u3 peak throughput).

records.claimSummary: Pricing rules read price lists from Redis.
records.conditionSummary: Price lists are cached for 300 seconds.
records.bindingReason: Reading from Redis stays true; the TTL bounds staleness.
records.notes: Intra-sentence. u6_n2 ('Caches price lists') has no TTL and no arrow to u4_n2.

records.claimSummary: The supplier feed adapter brings in restocks from suppliers.
records.conditionSummary: It polls the supplier API every 10 minutes.
records.bindingReason: Restocks still arrive via the adapter; the interval bounds latency.
records.notes: g4 takeaway and u5_a1 ('scheduled task') lack the interval. u5_n2 has no arrows.

notes: No records for overview facts (u1-u5), UI facts (u6-u8), 'only entry point'/'only module'/'only external system' exclusivity statements (u9, u25, u31, u45-u47), which are claims in their own right rather than limits on another claim, reading order (u41-u43), and u48 (no UI tests, standalone gap). u3 '3,000 per hour at peak' left without a record; u49 is attached to the ledger claim instead (r8, low confidence).
